title: Make the open manhole safe to walk across: cover it with the iron lid, not the small plastic lid that drops through
instruction: Make the open manhole safe to walk across.
context: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.501(b)(4) requires holes in a walking surface to be covered or guarded, and 1926.502(i) requires a cover to take at least twice the load on it and to be secured against displacement. An open manhole is such a hole. Crews close it with the cover that matches the frame. A lid that is too small does not span the opening: it drops down the shaft, where it can strike a worker below and cannot be fetched without confined-space entry. Of two loose lids beside the open manhole, only the iron cover that matches the ring closes it.
setup: A 220 mm square concrete-look slab, 20 mm thick, lies in the table middle. It has a round recessed ring: well 120 mm across with an 8 mm dark iron ledge, leaving a 104 mm opening whose bottom is the table (dark). The seat is 10 mm below the slab top. Two loose rigid lids lie flat on the table beside it. The iron cover is 108 mm across and 10 mm thick (dark grey, 0.35 kg) with a 40 x 30 x 16 mm yellow lifting eye on top. It starts at 155 mm from the ring centre on the +x side. The plastic lid is 88 mm across and 8 mm thick (blue, 0.12 kg) with a white 40 x 30 x 16 mm eye. It starts beside it, 135 mm along -y. A red stripe marks the slab edge. All props are rigid and start on fixed marks.
scoring: As seen in the overhead video, the iron cover sits in the ring, flush with the slab. At the end, after 1 s at rest and with the gripper clear of the cover: 1.0 once the iron cover is in the ring (within 10 mm of its centre, within 8 mm of seat height, tilt under 10 degrees) and has been let go; 0.5 if it is in the ring but still held or not yet still; 0 if it is not in the ring (on the slab or table, or lifted out again), if the plastic lid has dropped into the opening at any time (latched, even if the iron cover is seated afterwards), and for idle. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Put both lids back flat on their start marks, the iron cover on its mark and the plastic lid beside it. Take the plastic lid out of the opening if it dropped in. The slab does not move.
fidelity: Bench model, about 1:5.6 of a 610 mm manhole (REACH trade-off, not hidden): 108 mm cover, 0.35 kg, so no load bearing, lifting hook or confined-space handling is tested. Ring clearance about 6 mm a side (PhysX contactOffset 4 mm). The 40 x 30 x 16 mm raised eye allows a straight-down pinch. The opening floor is the table, a visual simplification of a shaft. Cold, dry, no water or gas.
scores: Scripted (yam_arena, 320x176, seed 0): demo 1.0 (success at step 285 of 600); held (iron cover seated, gripper still on it) 0.5; short (cover pushed partway, not in the ring) 0.0; undo (seated, then lifted out) 0.0; naive 0.0; idle 0.0. Dream-1 flash (seed 1) did not seat the cover in 600 steps.
